description: Pre-registered test set for LIME attribution audit. DO NOT MODIFY after initial commit.

inputs.text: I am not entirely unhappy with this result.
inputs.rationale: Double negation; LIME may attribute to 'unhappy' and miss 'not'

inputs.text: This is not good.
inputs.rationale: Simple negation. Minimal pair with input 3. Does LIME weight 'not'?

inputs.text: This is good.
inputs.rationale: Minimal pair baseline for input 2. Expect strong positive attribution to 'good'

inputs.text: I would not recommend this to anyone.
inputs.rationale: Negation + strong negative downstream. Does 'not' or 'recommend' get more weight?

inputs.text: Nothing about this experience was disappointing.
inputs.rationale: Negation of a negative. Semantically positive but full of negative-surface tokens

inputs.text: The movie was terrible but I loved every minute of it.
inputs.rationale: 'terrible' vs 'loved' - contradictory lexical signals. Which does LIME pick?

inputs.text: Excellent packaging, but the product itself is useless.
inputs.rationale: Positive word first, negative verdict expected. Does LIME over-weight 'Excellent'?

inputs.text: I love how badly this was designed.
inputs.rationale: Sarcastic use of 'love'. LIME likely attributes to 'love' as positive

inputs.text: Fine.
inputs.rationale: Single word, minimal context. Already flagged in README as unstable for LIME

inputs.text: Absolutely phenomenal waste of my time.
inputs.rationale: 'Absolutely phenomenal' are strong positive cues but sentence is negative

inputs.text: It was okay, I guess.
inputs.rationale: Lukewarm/ambiguous. Near decision boundary. Expect high LIME instability

inputs.text: That is one way to do it.
inputs.rationale: Pragmatically neutral-to-negative but lexically flat

inputs.text: I have seen worse.
inputs.rationale: Faint praise; could go either way

inputs.text: The service was exactly what I expected.
inputs.rationale: Ambiguous: could mean good or bad depending on expectations

inputs.text: It is what it is.
inputs.rationale: Tautology, no sentiment content. Tests LIME on near-zero-signal input

inputs.text: ngl this slaps fr fr no cap
inputs.rationale: Internet slang / Gen-Z. Far from SST-2 movie reviews

inputs.text: The patient presents with acute exacerbation of chronic symptoms.
inputs.rationale: Clinical language. No sentiment content; OOD for SST-2

inputs.text: Revenue increased 12% YoY driven by strong Q4 performance.
inputs.rationale: Financial/earnings language. Positive facts but not sentiment-positive

inputs.text: lmaooo this is so bad its good
inputs.rationale: Informal internet speak. Mixed signals plus typos

inputs.text: Per the attached memo, please advise on next steps.
inputs.rationale: Corporate email tone. Neutral, formal, zero sentiment

inputs.text: This is the best product I have ever purchased.
inputs.rationale: Unambiguously positive. LIME should be stable and faithful here

inputs.text: Terrible experience, complete waste of money.
inputs.rationale: Unambiguously negative. Expect stable negative attributions

inputs.text: I absolutely love everything about this.
inputs.rationale: Strong positive. Baseline for stability measurement

inputs.text: This is awful and I regret buying it.
inputs.rationale: Strong negative. Baseline for stability measurement

inputs.text: The quality exceeded all my expectations and I am thrilled.
inputs.rationale: Longer unambiguous positive. Tests stability on longer clear inputs

inputs.text: good good good good good
inputs.rationale: Repeated single token. LIME must distribute weight; tests degenerate case

inputs.text: The the the the movie was great.
inputs.rationale: Repeated function words. Does LIME attribute to 'the' or 'great'?

inputs.text: I think that maybe it could possibly be somewhat decent.
inputs.rationale: Heavily hedged. Many low-signal words dilute attribution

inputs.text: Amazing! Horrible! Amazing! Horrible!
inputs.rationale: Alternating contradictions. Near-random for bag-of-words approach
